topic-112-knowledge-evaluating-conversat.evolution: The representatives begin with goal-directed web navigation and working-memory structures. More recent papers introduce compositional workplace tasks, tool-oriented conversations, and planning–execution optimization. Experience-based approaches now distinguish action-level guidance from broader task skills and retrieve both using the current visual context.
openQuestions: How can agents recognize when a stored skill no longer fits the environment?
Which benchmarks measure durable improvement across tasks and sessions without rewarding memorized workflows?
topic-112-knowledge-evaluating-conversat.overview: Tool-using agents must turn a goal into actions that remain useful as an environment responds. This topic studies long-horizon planning, execution coordination, memory, and reusable skills. A representative training framework generates plans and alternative trajectories, then gives greater weight to examples where the proposed plan and actual execution agree.
topic-112-knowledge-evaluating-conversat.title: Agent Planning, Execution, and Reusable Experience
topic-112-knowledge-evaluating-conversat.whyItMatters: A plausible plan can fail through an impractical step, lost context, or deviation during execution. Evaluating agents across sessions and complex interfaces exposes these failures and tests whether stored experience improves future decisions rather than merely expanding memory.

topic-113-a-call-to-lagrangian-action-le.evolution: Early representatives learn qualitative or example-based descriptions of dynamics. Later work develops interpretable continuous-time models and neural controlled differential equations. Recent studies investigate decoder-free latent identification and spectral approaches with guarantees for specified classes of nonlinear systems, linking flexible modeling to explicit learnability conditions.
openQuestions: When are learned latent states identifiable and useful for control?
How can long-horizon errors be bounded when observation noise and environmental dynamics both change?
topic-113-a-call-to-lagrangian-action-le.overview: This topic learns hidden states and transition rules from sequences of observations. It includes stochastic state-space models, neural differential equations, irregularly sampled time series, and theoretical prediction guarantees. A representative probabilistic model learns dynamically relevant latent states without a parameterized reconstruction decoder, aiming to separate controllable structure from distracting visual detail.
topic-113-a-call-to-lagrangian-action-le.title: Latent Dynamical Systems and Continuous-Time Prediction
topic-113-a-call-to-lagrangian-action-le.whyItMatters: Useful dynamics models must represent what changes predictably, not just compress individual observations. Handling noise, irregular timing, and environmental variation is central to reliable forecasting and to models that can support intervention or control.

topic-114-a-difference-standardization-m.evolution: Early representatives use transferred discriminability, priors, and boosting. Later work develops minimax limits and multi-source weighting. Recent papers optimize source sample quantities, analyze feature dependence, and construct finite sets of candidate parameter-efficient adaptations to obtain informative few-shot generalization certificates.
openQuestions: How can relatedness be estimated reliably from very little target data?
Which guarantees remain useful when source tasks were selected adaptively or differ in unmeasured ways?
topic-114-a-difference-standardization-m.overview: Transfer learning uses knowledge from source tasks to improve learning on a target task with limited data. This cluster asks when transfer helps, how task similarity should be measured, and how much information to use from each source. Theoretical analyses relate achievable target error to source and target sample sizes, model capacity, and task relatedness.
topic-114-a-difference-standardization-m.title: Transferability, Source Selection, and Generalization Guarantees
topic-114-a-difference-standardization-m.whyItMatters: More source data is not automatically beneficial. Measuring transferability can help avoid negative transfer and allocate training effort toward sources whose information is relevant to the target rather than merely abundant.

topic-115-a-diffusion-model-of-joint-int.evolution: Early representatives study adaptive navigation and collision avoidance. Later work learns urban-driving policies and video world models from offline data. Recent approaches use flow matching, token prediction, and streaming vector graphs to improve interactive motion generation and computational efficiency, alongside benchmarks for spatiotemporal understanding.
openQuestions: How well do simulator improvements predict performance under unfamiliar real-world interactions?
How can models preserve physical and behavioral consistency during extended closed-loop rollouts?
topic-115-a-diffusion-model-of-joint-int.overview: Autonomous-driving models must represent roads, other agents, and the consequences of the vehicle's own actions. This topic combines imitation learning, trajectory prediction, generative world models, and closed-loop planning. A representative system learns a compact geometry-aware world model and policy from expert video, then predicts states and actions useful for driving.
topic-115-a-diffusion-model-of-joint-int.title: Driving World Models and Interactive Motion Planning
topic-115-a-diffusion-model-of-joint-int.whyItMatters: Plausible individual trajectories do not ensure realistic interaction over a long rollout. Evaluation must consider consistency with observed history, other agents' responses, physical feasibility, and the time available to make decisions.

topic-116-a-comprehensively-tight-analys.evolution: Earlier representatives estimate singular vectors and study radial-basis representations. Later work analyzes kernel approximation, matrix streams, and randomized projections. Recent papers extend density-based matrix computation and adaptive eigenvector estimation, with related spectral analyses appearing in structured sequence models.
openQuestions: Which access models remain realistic once data-loading costs are included?
How can approximation guarantees predict downstream learning quality rather than matrix error alone?
topic-116-a-comprehensively-tight-analys.overview: This topic develops efficient ways to estimate matrix structure, distances, and spectral quantities without processing every entry at full cost. Methods include random projections, low-rank approximation, streaming algorithms, and adaptive sensing. A representative approach uses kernel-density queries to accelerate operations on kernel matrices, with explicit error guarantees and computational lower bounds.
topic-116-a-comprehensively-tight-analys.title: Randomized Linear Algebra and Spectral Approximation
topic-116-a-comprehensively-tight-analys.whyItMatters: Many learning algorithms depend on large matrix operations that dominate memory or runtime. Structured access and approximation can make them feasible, but the savings depend on the required precision and on which information the access model actually provides.

topic-117-a-convex-relaxation-barrier-to.evolution: The representatives connect constrained optimization with input-convex networks and embedded optimization layers. Later work improves local Lipschitz certificates and verification domains. Recent architectures enforce input-dependent linear constraints directly, while related structured-network work considers how simplification affects implementable logic and accuracy.
openQuestions: Which architectural choices make useful properties easier to certify?
How can tighter guarantees scale without imposing unacceptable losses in prediction quality or inference speed?
topic-117-a-convex-relaxation-barrier-to.overview: Neural verification checks whether a network satisfies a property over an entire set of inputs, rather than only on tested examples. This topic includes robustness certificates, preimage bounds, differentiable optimization layers, and architectures that enforce constraints. A representative analysis shows limits of a broad convex-relaxation framework, separating solver quality from restrictions inherent in the relaxation.
topic-117-a-convex-relaxation-barrier-to.title: Neural Verification and Constraint-Satisfying Architectures
topic-117-a-convex-relaxation-barrier-to.whyItMatters: Empirical success cannot establish that every allowed input respects a required bound. Verification and structural constraints provide stronger assurances, but their scope, approximation gaps, and computational costs must be made explicit.

topic-118-a-closer-look-at-self-supervis.evolution: Early representatives investigate multiscale training and attention-based image sampling. Later work blends convolution with transformers and packs images at native resolutions. Recent papers examine fine-tuning components, large autoencoders, and windowed matrix operations that improve actual hardware throughput rather than relying only on nominal operation counts.
openQuestions: How can variable-resolution models allocate computation according to image content?
Which efficiency gains persist across hardware, image sizes, and dense downstream tasks?
topic-118-a-closer-look-at-self-supervis.overview: Vision models must combine local detail with relationships across large image regions. This cluster studies convolution–attention hybrids, efficient attention, variable-resolution processing, and large receptive fields. A representative transformer adds multiscale convolutional tokenization and parallel local processing so that spatial structure need not be learned entirely from data.
topic-118-a-closer-look-at-self-supervis.title: Efficient Vision Transformers and Multiscale Image Processing
topic-118-a-closer-look-at-self-supervis.whyItMatters: Images vary widely in size and aspect ratio, and computation grows quickly when every pixel or patch receives equal treatment. Architectural and implementation choices determine whether a model can retain fine detail while processing enough global context efficiently.

topic-119-textttfhaim-fully-homomorphic-.evolution: The representatives begin with privacy-preserving face detection, encrypted networks, and verifiable execution. Later work studies gradient leakage and posthoc privacy. Recent research scrutinizes corrupted model supply chains, hidden unlearning leakage, and fine-grained visual privacy detection in images and streams.
openQuestions: How can privacy guarantees remain meaningful when pretrained components are untrusted?
Which evaluations reveal sensitive information that ordinary utility or forgetting metrics overlook?
topic-119-textttfhaim-fully-homomorphic-.overview: This topic studies how information about users or training data can leak through learned systems and how to limit that exposure. Papers examine encrypted inference, collaborative representations, gradient reconstruction, private training, and unlearning. A representative framework connects a network's local sensitivity to formal privacy guarantees for representations shared with an inference provider.
topic-119-textttfhaim-fully-homomorphic-.title: Privacy-Preserving Inference and Information Leakage
topic-119-textttfhaim-fully-homomorphic-.whyItMatters: Failure of one reconstruction attack does not prove privacy. Formal guarantees, realistic threat models, and targeted leakage tests address different parts of the problem, including risks introduced by an untrusted pretrained model or by residual information after unlearning.
